title: feat(terrain): reach the horizon when zoomed out, and render flat when 3D buys nothing

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
## Symptom

Zoomed out with 3D terrain (z8-9 and below), the ground ends in a disc well inside the
screen instead of reaching the horizon.

## Cause: the absolute view distance is zoom-independent

`ViewState::calculateViewDistance` lets an absolute distance in metres take over completely:

```cpp
float absolute = terrainOptions->getViewDistance();
if (absolute > 0) {
    return absolute * Const::WORLD_SIZE / Const::EARTH_CIRCUMFERENCE;
}
factor = terrainOptions->getViewDistanceFactor();
```

Tangram's factor rule (`2 * cameraDistance / cos(pitch + fovy/2)`, capped at 127 tile widths)
is **scale-invariant** — `cameraDistance` is proportional to `2^-zoom`, so the drawn ground keeps
the same size on screen at every zoom. An absolute distance in metres does not, so it becomes
the binding constraint as soon as the camera is high enough.

Derived, 1080x2400, fovy 60, tilt 90, z8:

| | |
|---|---|
| camera height | ~1270 km |
| tangram factor rule | ~2500 km |
| `VIEW_DISTANCE_METERS` (android-dev demo default) | 170 km |

~15x short. The SDK default is `_viewDistance = 0` (factor rule), so this affects apps that pin
metres, the style property `terrain-max-visible-distance`, and the demo.

Only tile culling is cut (`TileLayer::_maxVisibleDistance`); the far plane is `max(far, viewDistance)`
and is never shortened. That matches the symptom — the ground stops, the sky/background continues.

Cheap A/B:

```sh
adb shell am broadcast -a com.massifmaps.MassifDemo.CONFIG --es viewDistanceMeters 0 --es zoom 8
```

### Fix

Take `max(absolute, factorRule)` instead of letting the absolute value win outright, in
`ViewState::calculateViewDistance` and in `TileLayer::calculateVisibleTiles` for the style's
`terrain-max-visible-distance`. The absolute distance exists to **extend** the view when the camera
is close to the terrain, never to shorten it when zoomed out. The factor rule keeps the app's own
factor, so a deliberate `0.5` is still respected.

Behaviour change, no API change.

## Second part: auto-flatten at low zoom and at tilt 90

Beyond the view distance, 3D terrain buys nothing once the displacement is sub-pixel (zoomed out)
or seen straight down, and still costs the drape RTT, the terrain passes and the elevation fetches.
Mapbox-style: switch to flat automatically, remember what the app asked for, make it configurable.

### Criterion — parallax, not a zoom threshold

```
parallaxPx ~= halfDiagonalPx * heightRangeMeters * exaggeration / cameraDistanceMeters
flatten = parallaxPx < AutoFlattenParallax  ||  tilt >= AutoFlattenTilt
```

Derived, Alps (4 km height range), 1300 px half-diagonal: **z8 -> ~4 px**, **z13 -> ~130 px**.
One knob covers zoom and tilt together and adapts to flat country for free. Hysteresis is mandatory
(restore at 1.5x, tilt -2 deg) or it thrashes on the boundary. The tilt term is separate because at
z13 top-down the parallax is still large but the 3D buys nothing.

### Two levers, very different price

**L1 - exaggeration to 0.** `ElevationManager::setExaggeration` bumps only the *global* version, not
the data version: heights are GPU-side and CPU display heights scale by the same factor. Zero
re-decode, animatable, pixel-identical to flat. No perf win.

**L2 - terrain off.** Drops the terrain passes, the drape and the elevation fetches. Today
`TileLayer::loadData` compares `_terrainEnabled` and calls `clearTileCaches(true)` +
`resetTileTransformer()`, which drops the *visible* cache too: blank map until every visible tile is
re-decoded.

Plan: ramp L1 to 0, then flip L2 while the two renderings are already identical.

### L2 without the re-decode

The cache blowup is not required. Keep `TileLayer::loadData` and `resetTileTransformer` reading the
app's `isEnabled()`, so the transformer and every decoded tile stay put; move only the render and
cull consumers to a new internal `isActive()`.

| Site | Reads |
|---|---|
| `TileLayer::loadData` cache compare, `TileLayer::resetTileTransformer` | `isEnabled()` — unchanged |
| `MapRenderer` terrain height range | `isEnabled()` — the criterion needs it |
| `TileLayer::calculateVisibleTiles` LOD, `MapRenderer` terrain depth source, `TileRenderer`, `SkyRenderer`, `BillboardPlacementWorker`, `VectorLayer`, `HillshadeRasterTileLayer` | `isActive()` |

`vt::GLTileRenderer::setTerrainMode` is a live flag (only `updateTerrainSkirts()`, no cache
invalidation), so flipping it per frame is safe. The effective flag has to join the re-cull
change-detect block in `loadData` so a still map re-culls.

Tiles decoded in terrain mode render correctly flat: displacement is GPU-side and the only
decode-time difference is subdivision density — extra triangles, harmless.

### Exaggeration ownership

`TerrainOptions::_exaggeration` keeps the app's requested value; the `ElevationManager` receives
`requested * (1 - flatten)`. Needed either way: the parallax test reads the height range through
`getDisplayHeightRange`, which is already exaggeration-scaled, so ramping the app's own value would
zero the criterion and the map could never un-flatten.

Camera clearance needs no change — at exaggeration 0, `getDisplayHeight` returns 0 and the clamp
falls back to sea level on its own.

### API

On `TerrainOptions` (mirrored in `all/modules/*.i`, needs a SWIG regen):

- `setAutoFlattenParallax(float px)` — 0 disables
- `setAutoFlattenTilt(float degrees)` — 0 disables
- `setAutoFlattenDuration(float seconds)` — default 0.3
- `isFlattened()` read-back

All default to **off**, so upgrading changes nothing until an app opts in. The android-dev demo turns
them on; flip the SDK defaults once device-verified.

## Also in scope

- android-dev: `AUTO_FLATTEN_*` in `DemoConfig`, `--es autoFlatten` / `--es autoFlattenTilt`,
  `DemoLive` keys, `DemoPanel` sliders
- `docs/internals/rendering/04-terrain.md`: the two levers, why exaggeration to 0 needs no
  re-decode, the parallax formula, the hysteresis, the view-distance `max()` rule
- `docs/internals/rendering/11-tangram-diff.md`: tangram has no absolute view distance at all
  (`core/src/view/view.cpp`), and their zoom-dependent lever is `m_maxPitchStops` (a max-pitch
  ramp over zoom), not a mode switch — we picked parallax instead
- `TerrainOptions.h`: the `getMinZoom` doc block is orphaned above `getDrapeResolution`

## Risks

- **Label re-anchor per ramp frame.** `setExaggeration` bumps the global version, so `TileRenderer`'s
  `scaleOnly` path calls `invalidateLabelElevation()` every frame for the length of the ramp. Cost
  unmeasured; may need suppressing while ramping.
- **Terrain-decoded tiles with `terrainMode` false** is an untested combination — the one thing that
  could blink.
- The open terrain-toggle crash in the backlog may live on exactly this path.

## Done means

- z8: the ground fills the screen instead of a 170 km disc
- tilt sweep 60 -> 90 and zoom sweep z12 -> z7: no blank map, no visible seam, no thrash at the
  boundary
- frame time at z13 / tilt 90 measurably lower
- verified on device, not on the emulator

## Not verified

No build and no device run yet. Every number above is derived from the formulas in
`ViewState::calculateViewDistance` and the camera model, not measured.

title: Labels: lift a POI onto the roof of the building it stands on (mapbox symbol-z-elevate)

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
POIs sit at ground level even when they belong to a building that is drawn 30 m tall. At tilt, the
icon and its name float in front of the facade instead of standing on the roof. mapbox solves this
with `symbol-z-elevate` (newer: `symbol-elevation-reference`): a symbol whose anchor falls inside a
building footprint is raised to that building's roof.

The plumbing for this already exists here, so the lift itself is close to free.

## Why it is cheap

- Label anchors already carry a per-point Z and a re-anchor pass with dirty tracking
  ([`Label::updateElevation`](https://github.com/massif-maps/massif-maps-libs/blob/develop/vt/src/vt/Label.cpp), `_elevationDirty` in `vt/src/vt/Label.h`).
- Label vertex data is rebuilt **every frame** (`GLTileRenderer::renderLabels` calls
  `Label::calculateVertexData` with no cache and no dirty gate), so a per-frame lift term costs one
  multiply-add per label.
- Buildings already **grow** with the tile blend — the `POLYGON3D` draw sets
  `uHeightScale = blend / heightScale * coordScale` in `GLTileRenderer::renderTileGeometry`. Lifting
  the label by `roofHeight * tileBlend` makes the POI ride the roof up as it grows: no popping, no
  animation machinery to add.

Footprints and their heights are already handed to `TileLayerBuilder::createPolygon3DProcessor` at
decode time (from `BuildingSymbolizer`), so the only new work is keeping them long enough to answer
one point-in-polygon query per opted-in POI, per tile.

## Scope of this issue

Anchor lift only. **Occlusion is explicitly out** (see below).

### Style knob

`marker-elevate-to-building: true` / `text-elevate-to-building: true`, translated to the symbolizer
property `elevate-to-building`. Same shape as the existing fork property
`marker-allow-overlap-same-feature-id`. Default false, so nothing changes until a style opts in.

### Decode side (`libs-massif`)

1. `cartocss/src/cartocss/CartoCSSMapnikTranslator.cpp` — map `text-elevate-to-building` and
   `marker-elevate-to-building` to `elevate-to-building`.
2. `mapnikvt` — `BoolProperty _elevateToBuilding` + `bindProperty` in `TextSymbolizer` and
   `MarkersSymbolizer`, threaded through the text/point processors like
   `_allowOverlapSameFeatureId`.
3. Per-tile footprint registry: record `(bbox, ring, height)` in `createPolygon3DProcessor`, shared
   across the tile's layer builders.
4. Resolve as a **post-pass at the end of the tile decode**, not inline — otherwise it depends on
   the building layer being decoded before the label layer, which the style order happens to give
   but does not guarantee. Uniform grid over the tile, point-in-ring per opted-in POINT label,
   height stored in metres on the `TileLabel`. Point labels only; line labels never lift.
5. Lift = **eave height** (`height`). Roof apex for pyramidal/gabled roofs is a known gap.

### Render side (`vt`)

6. The lift belongs to the **`TilePoint`, not the Label**. A merged `globalId` label holds one point
   per tile, each over a different building or none; a per-Label value picks the wrong one after a
   tile-set change.
7. **One anchor accessor** returning `tilePoint.position + normal * (lift * liftBlend)`.
   `calculateCenter`, `calculateEnvelope`, `calculateVertexData` and placement construction must all
   read it. If the culler and the draw path read different anchors, labels collide against ghost
   positions — this is the invariant of the change.
8. `liftBlend` = the blend of `label->getTileId()`, from a tileId to blend map built once per frame
   in the prepare loop.
9. `updateElevation` keeps its current meaning (it writes terrain height into `position(2)`); the
   lift is added on top by the accessor. That way it also works with terrain OFF, where
   `_labelElevationProvider` is null and the re-anchor loop never runs.

### SDK side (`all/native`)

10. Metres-to-world scale plumbed next to `setLabelElevationProvider` in
    `renderers/TileRenderer.cpp`, so `vt` stays projection-agnostic. No new public option class —
    the knob is a style property.

### Demo

11. `DemoConfig.bldPoiLift` (default false), written into the inline style's marker/text block, and
    the key added to the `DemoLive` **style-rebuild** list — a style knob needs a re-decode, not an
    option apply.

## Verification

- `clang++ -fsyntax-only` on every touched translation unit.
- Device A/B:
  `--es demo composite --es style inline --es styleLight true --es bld3d true --es tilt 60 --es zoom 17 --es bldPoiLift true|false`,
  plus one `pm clear` run to watch a cold tile fade in and confirm the lift tracks the growth.

## Docs (same commit)

- `docs/internals/rendering/06-labels.mdx` — mechanism, the single-accessor invariant, the blend
  sync, known gaps.
- `docs/features/label-styling.md` — the property.
- `docs/internals/rendering/11-tangram-diff.md` — comparison with mapbox `symbol-z-elevate`.

## Known gaps shipped with it

- **No occlusion.** A POI lifted onto a roof behind a taller building will draw over that building.
  The existing label occlusion test rays against the TERRAIN only; testing against extrusions needs
  a ray-vs-extrusion query or a depth sample, and is the expensive half of the feature. Separate
  issue.
- Eave height only — a steep pyramidal or gabled roof will bury the label slightly.
- Footprints from the same tile only.
- A building filtered out by zoom drops its POIs back to the ground.
- At tilt 0 the lift is invisible by construction.

title: Facade API: a six-verb ABI over the SDK, with events and a C binding for RN / NativeScript / WASM

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
The SDK exposes **495 Java proxy classes** across **221 SWIG modules**, and every capability is an object you construct and wire by hand. That buys two things worth keeping — objects usable *outside* a map (a `TileDataSource` driving an app's own tile server or feeding a webview), and one source/decoder shared by several maps — but it costs JNI weight, maintenance, and day-to-day ergonomics. Features tied hard to the map (fog, sky, terrain, light) are the worst fit: each is its own options class with its own setters.

This adds a **second, opt-in API surface**: a **six-verb ABI** over the existing objects, with JSON specs and string ids, plus an `extern "C"` binding so React Native / NativeScript modules and a future WASM build drive the SDK without JNI.

Nothing is removed. Every existing class stays public and unchanged, and the facade hands the real typed object back on demand.

## Requirements

The design targets these, and every decision below traces back to one of them:

1. **All of the SDK reachable through a minimum of new API.**
2. **No capability regressions.** Things that were easy because you held an object — reordering a layer you just removed — must stay easy when you hold only an id.
3. **Events everywhere, with metadata, cheaply.** C ABI, Java, Obj-C and whatever comes next; a clicked vector-tile feature must be reachable without serialising a 5000-point line.
4. **Choose the delivery thread per subscription.** UI thread or origin thread. Not possible today.
5. **Pluggable** — new features, removed features, third-party extensions.
6. **The API must not know about style properties.** A new style property is zero work.
7. **Multi-map.**
8. **The MapView stays native** (Java/Obj-C owns the GL surface and input), and the C ABI must still plug into it for RN/NativeScript.
9. **Decoders and custom asset packages** (`DirAssetPackage`) must have a natural home.
10. **Maintenance:** adding a feature must not mean touching binding code.

## Measured baseline

What the current binding surface costs (Android arm64, Release, full profile):

| | |
|---|---|
| SWIG modules (`all/modules/*.i`) | 221 |
| Java proxy classes | 495 |
| exported `Java_*` symbols | 3496 |
| generated wrapper C++ / Java | 182k / 53k lines |
| **Java side dex** | **780 KB** |
| **native side** | wrappers ~5 % of `.text` (~335 KB) + 410 KB `.dynsym`/`.dynstr` ≈ **745 KB of 11.4 MB (6.5 %)** |
| build time | 14 % of a full build is wrapper compile |

Source: [build-and-size.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/build-and-size.md). `RegisterNatives` was already built and measured as **+131 KB worse** — that lever is dead.

**This work costs bytes, it does not save them** (see [Size](#size)). The 745 KB + 780 KB only comes back later, if a `facade` profile stops wrapping the old classes. Out of scope here — the analysis is in [The future](#the-future-if-it-becomes-the-single-true-api).

## Two things already in the tree

- `Variant` ([core/Variant.h](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/core/Variant.h)) — picojson-backed JSON value, already wrapped, with `toString()` emitting JSON.
- `MBVectorTileDecoder::setJSONStyleParameters(std::string)` — precedent for "pass a JSON blob, don't rebuild the tree over JNI".

And the load-bearing one: **the invalidation channel is already string-keyed.** `Options::notifyOptionChanged("MainLightColor")` is dispatched per name in [MapRenderer.cpp:3296](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/renderers/MapRenderer.cpp#L3296), with prefix rules for `TerrainOptions*` / `FogOptions*`. A facade that forwards to the existing setter inherits today's exact redraw granularity for free — `set(map, "fog.rangeStart", 1.2)` costs precisely what `fogOptions.setRangeStart(1.2)` costs.

## The ABI: six verbs

```c
mm_obj create (mm_ctx, const char* kind, const char* id, const char* json);
int    destroy(mm_ctx, const char* kind, const char* id);
int    set    (mm_obj target, const char* path, /* typed value */);
int    get    (mm_obj target, const char* path, /* out */);
int    update (mm_obj target, const char* json);                 // batch set, validate then apply
int    call   (mm_obj target, const char* method, const char* json, char** out);
mm_sub on     (mm_obj target, const char* event, mm_handler h, const char* optsJson, void* ud);
int    off    (mm_sub subscription);                             // see Unsubscribing
int    off_event(mm_obj target, const char* event);
int    off_all  (mm_obj target);

// same concept as call, different completion - see Async
int call_async(mm_obj target, const char* method, const char* json,
               mm_handler onDone, const char* optsJson, void* ud);

uint32_t mm_version(void);   // so an embedder can refuse a mismatched SDK
```

**Eleven functions, six concepts.** The invariant is that a *feature* never adds an ABI function -
`update`, `off`, `call_async` and `mm_version` are mechanisms, and the set of mechanisms is closed.
A new source type, option, service or style property still adds nothing.

Everything else stops being API and becomes **data**:

| what you want | how |
|---|---|
| add a layer | `create("layer","base",{map:"m1",type:"vector",source:"osm",style:"osmStyle"})` |
| reorder | `set(layer,"index",2)` |
| route | `call(router,"route",{…})` |
| style parameter | `set(style,"buildings",true)` |
| fog | `set(map,"fog.rangeStart",1.2)` |
| a plugin's own source type | `create("source","x",{type:"my-plugin-type",…})` |

**The invariant that gives requirement 10: adding a feature never adds an ABI function.** It adds a row in a generated table or an entry in a factory. The C ABI, the WASM surface and every binding stay frozen at six.

### The closed-sugar rule

Six verbs are the **ABI**, not what an app types. Java/Obj-C get a hand-written convenience layer on top — and that layer is **closed**:

> The sugar covers only concepts that will not grow — map lifecycle, camera, layer ordering, registry CRUD, event subscription. Roughly 30 methods, written once per platform. A **new feature** (source type, option, service, style property) arrives as *data* through the existing sugar and never adds a method. If a feature seems to need a new sugar method, fix the spec instead.

This is a rule, not a preference. Without it, hand-written sugar reintroduces exactly the per-platform maintenance requirement 10 exists to delete.

## Namespaces, ids and lifetime

Ids collide **only within a kind** — a source and a layer both named `osm` is fine, as in mapbox. Sources, styles, element styles and services are **global**; layers are **per-map**.

Per-map is a technical fact: `Layer` holds a single `_mapRenderer` weak_ptr and the "already attached to a different map" guard is commented out in this fork ([Layer.cpp:189](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/layers/Layer.cpp#L189)), so adding one layer to two maps silently rebinds it.

**Requirement 2 — the id *is* the handle, and it outlives the draw stack:**

- `set(layer, "index", 2)` — reorder without removing. Most of the "I lost the object" cases never arise.
- `call(map, "detachLayer", {id})` / `attachLayer{id, index}` — out of the draw stack, still in the registry, re-attach by id.
- `destroy("layer", id)` — detaches it from its map first, then frees it. Destroying an attached
  layer without detaching would leave the draw stack holding a dead object.

Today you must hold the object to put it back; here you hold a string you chose. Moving a layer between maps is destroy + create, for the `_mapRenderer` reason above.

Registry rules:

- create an id that exists with an **identical** spec → reuse (that is the two-maps-share-a-source case)
- same id, **different** spec → throw, never silent replace
- `destroy("source", id)` unregisters the **name**; the object survives while any map still holds it
- headless is the same registry, no map involved
- `register(kind, id, obj)` adopts an object built with the old API, so the two APIs never fork

## Specs and factories

Source composition nests, because the SDK's sources compose heavily and mapbox has no equivalent:

```json
{"type":"persistent-cache","path":"/sdcard/c.db","capacity":52428800,
 "source":{"type":"http","url":"https://…/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf","subdomains":["a","b"]}}
```

Inline object = anonymous child; string = registry reference. Covers `combined`, `merged-mbvt`, `multi`, `ordered`, `memory-cache` identically.

**Requirement 9 — decoders and asset packages.** Asset packages become **URI schemes** resolved by the factory: `dir:///sdcard/osm` → `DirAssetPackage`, `zip://osm.zip` → `ZippedAssetPackage`, `asset://…` → `AssetPackage`.

```js
create("style", "osm", {type:"cartocss", source:"dir:///sdcard/osm"})
create("layer", "base", {map:"m1", type:"vector", source:"tiles", style:"osm"})
```

A custom `AssetPackage` subclass uses the director slot, or `register("style", id, obj)` hands in one built the old way.

The 16 `*StyleBuilder` classes are pure attribute bags, so the same generator that builds the property table builds their spec parser:

```js
create("elementStyle", "pin", {type:"marker", size:30, color:"#f00", bitmap:"asset://pin.png"})
```

## Property paths

`swigpp-*.py` already parses the attribute macros. **717 declarations** across the tree, in six forms, and the table needs a *kind* per row — not every attribute is a scalar:

| form | count | kind | settable from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `%attribute` | 386 | scalar | number / bool / enum constant |
| `%attributeval` | 150 | struct | JSON array or object (`MapRange`, `MapBounds`, `MapPos`) |
| `%attributestring` | 126 | string **or** object ref | string, or a registry id |
| `!attributestring_polymorphic` | 49 | object ref | a registry id |
| `%staticattribute` / `…string` / `…_polymorphic` | 6 | static | — |

Emitted as a sorted static array, binary-searched, no `std::map`, no allocation:

```cpp
{ "fog.rangeStart", PK_SCALAR, PT_FLOAT, FogOptions_setRangeStart, FogOptions_getRangeStart },
```

Only attributes get paths. Non-attribute methods (`TileLayer::clearTileCaches(bool)`) are reached with `call(layer, "clearTileCaches", json)`.

**Requirement 6 — three kinds of "style property", all already zero work:**

- **CartoCSS `param::` values** — already dynamic. `setStyleParameter(name, value)` takes any name. Add one to a style, nothing to do anywhere.
- **CartoCSS paint properties** (`line-color`) — live in the style, never in the API. The facade is over CartoCSS, so it never learns them.
- **SDK option properties** (`fog.rangeStart`) — generated from the attribute macros. Adding a setter makes the path appear on the next build. Never hand-maintained.

## Async

Seven ABI functions, still six concepts: `call_async` is `call` with a different completion, not a
new idea. It needs **no new machinery**, because both halves already exist:

- **Execution** — `CancelableThreadPool` (`execute(task, priority)`, `cancelAll()`), which the SDK
  already runs for layers and tiles.
- **Completion delivery** — the same `mm_handler` and the same delivery-mode dispatcher as `on(...)`,
  so a result lands on the UI thread when asked. That is exactly what embedders hand-roll today.

```java
map.callAsync(hillshade, "elevations", posJson,
              new EventOptions().delivery(Delivery.UI),
              (t, e, payload) -> { double[] elev = payload.getArray("elevations"); return true; });
```

Two capabilities that come with it and cannot be had today:

- **Cancellation.** `CancelableTask` is already first-class in the pool. A Java thread running
  `getElevations` cannot be cancelled; an SDK task can — `call(requestHandle, "cancel")`. Panning
  away mid-profile stops costing.
- **One pool, not N.** Embedders currently spawn their own threads for elevation, geocoding and
  routing on top of the SDK's tile and cull pools. Inside the SDK they contend under one budget
  instead of fighting it.

**What is async:** elevation profiles, geocoding and reverse geocoding, routing and route matching,
package download, and source creation that touches disk (`mbtiles` open, `pmtiles` header fetch) —
every one of them Promise-wrapped by an embedder today. Everything else stays synchronous;
`set`/`get` on options must not become async.

## Events

The hardest part of the design, and the one with the most requirements pointing at it (3, 4, 7, 8).

### One shape everywhere

```c
typedef int (*mm_handler)(void* ud, mm_obj target, const char* event, mm_obj payload);
```

The payload is a **handle**, not a serialised blob. Nothing materialises until a path is read:

```c
mm_get_d  (payload, "clickPos.lon", &lon);          // scalar, no alloc
mm_get_str(payload, "properties.name", buf, cap);   // one key, no JSON parse of the bag
mm_get_str(payload, "geometryGeoJSON", buf, cap);   // only if you actually want it
```

A 5000-point clicked line costs nothing unless you read its geometry, and then it is a `double[]` memcpy (see [Bulk geometry](#bulk-geometry)), not JSON.

### What the payload must expose

Taken from a real NativeScript handler that does all of this by hand today. Every row is a **derived** path that does not exist yet:

| path | replaces | work |
|---|---|---|
| `featurePos` | `getFeaturePosIndex()` + MultiPoint downcast + `getCenterPos()` | resolve the MultiPoint index in C++ — `getFeatureClickPos()` explicitly does not |
| positions in a chosen projection | `layer.getDataSource().getProjection()` + `toWgs84` + `fromWgs84` | per-subscription `projection`, applied before delivery |
| `geometryGeoJSON` | construct `GeoJSONGeometryWriter`, `setSourceProjection`, `writeGeometry` | one call, source projection preset from the layer |
| `properties` / `properties.<key>` | `getProperties().toString()` + `JSON.parse` | dotted walk over the `Variant`; no parse to read one key |
| `geometryType` | `/MultiPoint/.test(geometry.constructor.name)` | a real type string — regex-matching a class name is a gap in today's API, not a preference |

That handler goes from ~45 lines to ~12, with no JNI object traffic at all.

### Lifetime

**Valid until your handler returns.** `retain`/`release` to keep it longer.

Phrased that way deliberately: it reads identically whether the handler ran inline or three milliseconds later on the UI thread. For queued delivery the SDK retains at enqueue and releases after the handler returns.

### Delivery thread (requirement 4)

Per subscription: `ORIGIN` (today's behaviour — GL thread, tile thread, whatever produced it), `UI`, `BACKGROUND`.

Both platforms hop in **pure C inside the SDK**, no binding code and no JNI on the path:

- **Android** — at init (on the UI thread, from the `MapView` constructor) take `ALooper_forThread()` and attach an eventfd. Any thread posts by writing to it. No `JNIEnv`, no attach/detach, no global ref.
- **iOS / macOS** — `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), …)`.

`mm_set_ui_dispatcher` exists as an **override**, for NativeScript/RN landing callbacks on their JS thread, and for desktop or WASM loops:

```c
void mm_set_ui_dispatcher(mm_ctx, void (*post)(void* ud, void (*fn)(void*), void* arg), void* ud);
```

### Coalescing

Per subscription. With `coalesce: true`, an event already queued for that subscription has its payload replaced (old one released) rather than a second being enqueued. That is what stops a UI-thread `moved` handler flooding the looper. Discrete events default to `false`.

### Unsubscribing

`on` returns a **subscription handle**, so it can be undone. Three removals, because all three come
up: one handler, everything for an event, everything for a target.

```c
mm_sub s = on(map, "vectortile.click", handler, opts, ud);
off(s);                          // this one
off_event(map, "vectortile.click");  // every handler of that event on that target
off_all(map);                    // every subscription on that target
```

`mm_sub` is a handle with the same 20-bit index / 12-bit generation encoding as an object handle, so
calling `off` twice is an error rather than removing whatever took the slot.

Four rules that are easy to get wrong and expensive to fix later:

- **Destroying a target removes its subscriptions.** Otherwise the first `destroy` on a map with a
  click handler is a use-after-free. This is not optional and it is not the app's job.
- **Removal from inside a handler is deferred.** Calling `off` while the dispatcher is iterating
  that target's handlers is the classic iterator-invalidation crash. The subscription is marked
  dead, skipped for the rest of the pass, and reaped afterwards.
- **A queued payload can outlive its target.** With `delivery: UI` the handler runs later, and the
  map may be gone by then. The payload handle stays valid - it is retained - but the *target*
  handle it was delivered with can be stale, and a handler that dereferences it has to cope.
- **Two consuming handlers on one event resolve by registration order**, first to consume wins and
  the rest are skipped. Any other rule makes the outcome depend on a hash order.

`once(...)` is sugar: `on` plus `off` from inside the handler, under the deferred-removal rule.

### The sharp edge: a queued handler cannot consume

A handler that returns "consumed" stops propagation to lower layers — the SDK asks *now*, and a UI-delivered handler answers *later*. Waiting for it would block the GL thread on the main thread: a deadlock waiting to happen.

So `consume: true` **requires** `delivery: ORIGIN`, validated at registration:

```java
// throws at registration
map.on("vectortile.click", new EventOptions().delivery(Delivery.UI).consume(true), h);

// correct: answer synchronously, hop yourself for the UI work
map.on("vectortile.click", new EventOptions().consume(true), (t, e, payload) -> {
    boolean mine = "poi".equals(payload.getString("featureLayer"));
    if (mine) runOnUiThread(() -> showSheet(payload.getString("properties.name")));
    return mine;
});
```

`consume: false` — the default — is free to use any delivery.

### What it reads like

```java
map.on("vectortile.click",
       new EventOptions().delivery(Delivery.UI).projection("EPSG:4326"),
       (target, event, payload) -> {
    if (!"poi".equals(payload.getString("featureLayer"))) return false;
    long   id   = payload.getLong("featureId");
    String name = payload.getString("properties.name");
    double[] p  = payload.getPos("featurePos");
    return true;
});
```

## Value marshalling

`set`/`get` carry scalars and that is settled. `call` returns things scalars cannot express, and
two of them are load-bearing rather than exotic — both are on the headless path that already
works through the object API and must keep working through a handle.

| shape | how | why not JSON |
|---|---|---|
| scalar | typed `set`/`get` | — |
| struct (`MapPos`, `MapRange`) | JSON | small and rare |
| another object | registry id | identity matters, not contents |
| **binary** (`loadTile` → `TileData`/`BinaryData`) | **a handle, plus a copy-out** | base64 in JSON doubles a tile and forces a decode nobody asked for |
| **bulk numbers** (`getElevations` → `vector<double>`) | **a flat primitive array** | a 5000-point profile as JSON numbers is the cost P0.2 exists to remove |

```c
mm_obj  data = /* from call(source, "loadTile", {"z":..,"x":..,"y":..}) */;
size_t  n    = mm_data_size(data);
int     got  = mm_data_copy(data, buffer, capacity);   // nothing is copied until asked
int     len  = mm_call_array(layer, "elevations", posJson, doubles, capacity);
```

A handle rather than an eager byte array for the same reason event payloads are handles: a caller
that only wants the tile's size, or only the first elevation, should not pay for the rest.

**Converting to something an app can use** — an `ArrayBuffer`, `NSData`, a `byte[]`, a JSON string
— is the **binding's** job, not the ABI's. The ABI owes a handle, a length and a copy-out; each
platform's closed sugar layer wraps that in whatever is idiomatic. Putting the conversions in the
ABI would mean one entry point per target representation, which is exactly the growth the closed
sugar rule exists to prevent.

## Introspection

Not new verbs - these go through `call` on the context or the target, because they are queries, not
concepts:

```js
call(ctx,    "list",     {kind:"source"})   // -> ["osm", "dem", ...]
call(ctx,    "has",      {kind:"source", id:"osm"})
call(target, "describe")                    // -> {class, properties:[{path,type,readonly}], events:[...]}
call(target, "warnings")                    // what the last tolerant call dropped
```

`describe` costs almost nothing - the property table already holds every row and its type - and it
is what lets a NativeScript or WASM layer validate a spec before sending it, a debugger show what a
handle actually is, and a test assert that a rename did not silently drop a path. It is the reason
the table records a value type per row rather than just an accessor.

`warnings` matters because parsing is deliberately tolerant: a spec with a typo applies and logs.
Without a way to ask, a typo is invisible to anything but a human reading logcat.

### Round-tripping the state

```js
call(map, "toJSON")   // -> the specs that would rebuild this map
```

The mirror of `create`. Worth having for three reasons that keep coming up: saving and restoring a
map configuration, attaching the actual state to a bug report instead of a description of it, and
testing that `create(toJSON(x))` is a fixed point - which is the cheapest possible check that the
spec covers what the objects hold. Mapbox's `map.getStyle()` is the same idea.

## C ABI, and the native MapView (requirement 8)

`MapView` / `MSFMapView` keeps owning the GL surface and input — it must. It exposes `getNativeHandle()` → `mm_obj`, and an RN/NativeScript plugin passes that into the C ABI. One method per platform; everything else goes through the six verbs.

The context is explicit from day one, so WASM module scoping and test isolation work without a later break:

```c
mm_ctx mm_default_ctx(void);
```

Java/Swift/C# bind static `Massif.*` methods to the default context; internally it is a real `Context` object, so nothing is a raw global and `Massif.reset()` is trivial.

### Generic invoke — on by default

Six verbs plus specs cover the everyday work. **Requirement 1 — "all of the SDK"** — is made literally true by a table generated from the same parse, dispatched through one exported symbol:

```c
int mm_invoke(mm_obj h, const char* method, const char* jsonArgs, char** jsonOut);
```

~4000 entries × (name ~25 B + fn ptr 8 B + signature 4 B) ≈ **150 KB rodata**, and **one exported symbol** — no `.dynsym`/`.dynstr` bloat, where the current JNI layer pays 410 KB for that alone. **On by default** (+1.3 % of the library); a build flag strips it for size-critical artifacts.

## Directors

Six wrapped types are callbacks into app code, not data. Java/Swift keep SWIG directors unchanged; the C ABI needs a function-pointer slot each.

| director | payload | v1 |
|---|---|---|
| custom `TileDataSource` | tile bytes | **yes** — app-implemented sources are a real use case |
| `PostProcessEffect` | shader source string | **yes** |
| `ElevationDecoder` | decode function, numeric | **yes** |
| `ClusterElementBuilder` | a `VectorElement` per cluster | defer — needs element handles first |
| `CustomPopupHandler` | rendered `Bitmap` + hit test | defer — needs bitmap handles |
| listeners | events | covered above |

Every vtable starts with a `uint32_t size` so a plugin built against SDK 7 loads into SDK 8. That must land with the ABI, not after — it is also what makes requirement 5 (pluggable) work, via runtime-extensible factory tables.

## Vector elements

Objects are kept — `marker.setPos()` stays as fast as today — **plus** handles, so a NativeScript app with no objects can drive them:

```java
int h = Massif.addElement("pins", featureJson, "pinStyle");
Massif.setElementPos(h, lon, lat);          // typed, no JSON
VectorElement e  = Massif.getElement(h);    // handle -> object
int           h2 = Massif.handleOf(e);      // object -> handle
```

Same underlying object either way. Handles are `(generation << 20) | index` in a `uint32_t` — 1 M live, 4096 recycles before ABA, and it fits a JS number with no BigInt.

## Bulk geometry

`MapPos` is `double _x, _y, _z;` with no virtuals ([MapPos.h:156](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/core/MapPos.h#L156)), so `sizeof == 24`, standard layout, and `std::vector<MapPos>` **is already a contiguous `double[]`**.

Today Java reads it one point at a time: `MapPosVector.get(i)` is one JNI call plus two allocations **per point**. A 5000-point route is 5000 round trips — worse than any JSON path, which also answers "isn't a big JSON blob a problem for Valhalla/GeoJSON?": GeoJSON already crosses as a string ([GeoJSONVectorTileDataSource.h:99](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/datasources/GeoJSONVectorTileDataSource.h#L99)), `RoutingResult::getRawResult()` already returns the raw engine string, and the bottleneck is the *typed* path.

One universal layout (the flatgeobuf / deck.gl shape):

```java
double[] coords;      // x,y,z triples -- one SetDoubleArrayRegion memcpy
int[]    ringOffsets; // vertex index where each ring starts
int[]    partOffsets; // ring index where each part starts
```

Implementation: **add `toArray()` to the generated vector templates.** One generator change, and every existing method returning those types gets a bulk path.

It is not only `MapPosVector`. A real app pays this on `DoubleVector` (an elevation profile),
`StringVector` (asset names, category lists) and on vectors of *objects* such as
`GeocodingResultVector`. Scalars get a flat primitive array; object vectors need handles or a single
JSON dump, since there is nothing to memcpy.

## Evidence from a real app

Validated against [alpimaps](https://github.com/farfromrefug/alpimaps), a NativeScript app using the
SDK heavily through `@nativescript-community/ui-massifmaps`. What it does today:

**Nested source specs are real, not hypothetical.** `new PersistentCacheTileDataSource({ dataSource:
new HTTPTileDataSource({url}), capacity, databasePath })`, plus `Ordered(…)` and `Multi(…)`. The
construction is *already* an options object, so `create("source", id, {type:"persistent-cache", …,
source:{type:"http", url}})` is a 1:1 mapping. Its tile providers come from 901 lines of config
spread in with `...provider.sourceOptions` — with specs that config **is** the spec, and the plugin
needs no per-option binding. Today every option needs one.

**The per-element bridge cost is the top problem.** The navigation code walks a route polyline with
`positions.get(index)` twice per iteration, **on every GPS position update**, and carries a
`maxDistance` early-out whose comment says it exists because otherwise it "would cost thousands of
distances on every position" — a workaround for the bridge, not an algorithmic choice. With a flat
`double[]` the whole computation is pure JS over a typed array.

**Async is not optional.** Elevation profiles (`getElevationsAsync`), geocoding and routing are all
wrapped in Promises by the plugin, which runs its own worker threads because the SDK's
`HillshadeRasterTileLayer::getElevations` and the geocoding services are synchronous only. The
plugin also grew its own `toArray()` shim for `DoubleVector`. `callAsync` therefore lands with the
services in S3 rather than being deferred — its absence is what forces every embedder to thread.

**A consuming handler must answer synchronously.** Click handling dispatches to modules and gates on
a `handledByModules` boolean, which is exactly the `consume` semantics above — and why
`delivery: UI` with `consume: true` is rejected rather than merely discouraged.

**State events are frequent.** `onMapMove` / `onMapIdle` / `onMapStable` are all subscribed, so
per-subscription coalescing earns its place.

## Size

| item | estimate |
|---|---|
| context + handles + registry + six verbs + spec factories + C ABI | +60–110 KB `.text` |
| property table (717 rows, index switch, no per-property thunk) | +10–15 KB |
| event payload paths + dispatcher | +15–25 KB |
| generic `mm_invoke` table (on by default) | +150 KB |
| SWIG surface for the sugar | +15 KB native, +10 KB dex |
| **total** | **≈ +250–315 KB native (+2.5 %), +10 KB dex** |

All estimates, nothing built. Measure per slice.

## Plan

**P0 — standalone, no facade needed.** Each independently useful:

1. ~~`!enum` → `@IntDef` int constants~~ — **done**, [#152](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/pull/152)
2. `toArray()` on the vector templates — generator change; fixes the 5000-JNI-call route read that exists today
3. `beginBatch()` / `endBatch()` on the option classes — 8 fog properties currently fire 8 notifications and can request 8 cull passes
4. Variant-typed `setStyleParameter` overload

**S0 — property table generator.** Emits one row per attribute macro, with its kind. Everything downstream depends on it.
*Done when:* a row exists for every attribute declaration in the tree (counts match), it compiles, and `fog.rangeStart` / `map.tilt` / `terrain.exaggeration` resolve to the right setter.

**S1 — Context, handle table, registry, `set`/`get`.** The first thing that runs.
*Done when:* `set(map, "fog.rangeStart", 1.2)` changes the render **identically** to `fogOptions.setRangeStart(1.2f)` — A/B screenshot at a fixed terrain camera with fog on — and `mm_set_d` does the same from a C harness.

**S2 — specs and factories:** `create`/`destroy` over sources, styles, element styles, layers.

**S3 — `call` and `callAsync`,** including the binary and bulk returns above: layer/source operations, then services (routing, geocoding, search, package manager, elevation profiles) with `callArray` on P0.2's bulk layout. Async lands here, not later — see [Evidence from a real app](#evidence-from-a-real-app).

**S4 — events:** payload handles, derived paths, per-subscription projection, delivery thread,
coalescing, the `consume` rule, and **unsubscribe** — `off`, `off_event`, `off_all`, removal deferred
inside a handler, and subscriptions dying with their target.

**S5 — C ABI + generic invoke + vtable versioning.**

**S6 — the closed sugar layer**, Java then Obj-C.

**S7 — directors:** custom source, post-process, elevation decoder.

Documentation ships inside each slice. Roughly **45–60 dev days**; all estimates.

## The future: if it becomes the single true API

Not proposed here — the analysis, so the decision is made against numbers.

### Size: no, this is not a size lever

Ceiling if the entire old SWIG surface is deleted: **≈ −1.3 to −1.5 MB** across `.so` + dex, roughly **5–6 % of the 11.4 MB `.so`**. Ranked against what already exists:

| lever | returns | cost |
|---|---|---|
| ship the `standard` profile | **−3.42 MB (−30 %)** | zero — already built in CI |
| ship `lite` | **−4.38 MB (−38 %)** | zero |
| valhalla (22 % of `.text`) | multi-MB | prune / profile work |
| unwind metadata (1.69 MB, 16 % of the file) | up to ~1 MB | risky, needs a callback audit |
| **delete the old API surface** | **~0.7 MB native + 0.77 MB dex** | **a major version and a full migration for every app** |

Fourth-ranked and by far the most expensive. **Do not do this for bytes.**

### Refactor `all/native`? Only the boilerplate

202,410 lines, ~15 % of `.text`, mostly the render path. Two clusters are pure wrappability boilerplate the spec parser replaces: the 16 `*StyleBuilder` classes (**3243 of the 5945 lines in `all/native/styles/`, 55 %**) and the `*ClickInfo` family (2319 lines). Together ~5600 lines, **2.7 %**. Readability win, near-zero size win. Leave the rest alone.

### What a plugin can actually add

Three different things get called "a plugin adding a layer", and they are not equally possible.

**A new `"type"` over an SDK class — yes, and it works today.** `Spec::registerFactory(kind, type, fn)`
adds a type without displacing the kind's own factory; a type-level factory is found before the
SDK's fallback. `create("layer", "x", {"type":"my-tiles", …})` reaches it.

**Properties on a plugin's own class — needs one addition.** The property table is generated from
*this repo's* attribute macros, so a class the SDK has never seen resolves to `UNKNOWN_CLASS` and
`set` does nothing. It needs a runtime overlay:

```c
int mm_register_class(const char* cppClass, const char* base,
                      const mm_property* properties, uint16_t count);
```

Lookups would check the overlay before the generated array. Small, symmetric with the factory
registry, and without it a plugin's object is opaque to `set`/`get`/`describe`.

**A new C++ `Layer` SUBCLASS — possible, and the wrong thing to support.** Mechanically the facade
does not care: a factory returns `shared_ptr<void>` plus a class name and the registry stores it.
What breaks is everything around it:

- A `Layer` participates in `setComponents`, culling, draw order and the depth model, and its
  `onDrawFrame` takes `BillboardSorter&` and `ViewState&`. Subclassing it means compiling against
  the SDK's internal headers with a **matching compiler, STL and flags** — the exact fragility the
  C ABI exists to remove.
- Every renderer refactor becomes a breaking change for that plugin, which is the argument in
  [#147](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/147) for not exposing `Layer`.
- A NativeScript or WASM plugin cannot subclass a C++ class at all, so it would be a C++-only
  capability in an API whose point is to not be C++-only.

**The supported path is [#147](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/147)'s narrow draw
contract, reached as a type**: the SDK owns the `Layer` subclass, the plugin owns only a render
callback and its params struct.

```js
create("layer", "mine", {"type":"custom", "renderer": <vtable handle>})
```

So: **plugins add types, properties and draw callbacks — not classes.**

### Plugin API — yes, nearly free

The factory tables already exist; making them runtime-extensible is a small delta:

```c
int mm_register_source_type (mm_ctx, const char* type, const mm_source_vtable*);
int mm_register_layer_type  (mm_ctx, const char* type, const mm_layer_vtable*);
int mm_register_service_type(mm_ctx, const char* type, const mm_service_vtable*);
```

Works because no C++ type crosses the boundary. Needs: vtable versioning designed in with S5, iOS meaning **compile-time** registration (App Store), and a documented no-exceptions-across-the-boundary contract — no sandboxing.

### Custom C++ source yes; custom layer needs its own contract

A source vtable over the C ABI is strictly better than subclassing today, which pins you to the SDK's exact compiler and STL. A **layer** sits inside culling, draw order and the depth model, so exposing that as a vtable makes every render refactor breaking — it needs the narrow `CustomLayerInterface`-style contract in [#147](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/147).

### Dropping SWIG — possible, and the prize is not bytes

Only after the old API is gone. And the generator does **not** disappear: the property table, spec factories and the `mm_invoke` table all need a header parse, so it is a trade — the SWIG fork for ~2000 lines of libclang-based emitters we own. What makes it attractive: **236k lines of generated code gone**, **14 % of build time**, and the **`BUILDING.md` SWIG-fork prerequisite gone** — today nobody builds this SDK without a private fork checked out at a specific path. That is a contribution problem, not a size one.

## Open

- Nothing blocking. Decided: `off_event` and `off_all` are their own ABI functions, with the same
  signatures everywhere - a few extra entries is not the cost worth optimising. `create` throws.
- **Deferred directors** — `ClusterElementBuilder` and `CustomPopupHandler` need element and bitmap handles.

## Notes

- **mapbox-gl-js v3 is licensed under the Mapbox TOS, not BSD.** Its API shape and property naming are a reference; no code is copied.
- The facade is opt-in. Existing apps compile and behave identically.
- Errors throw. The one exception is an **unknown property name**, which is dropped with a warning so a config written against another SDK version still applies what it can; malformed JSON, unknown id and a bad value type on a known property all throw.
- `update(json)` validates the whole blob, then applies.
- Concurrency is per-call as today, plus batch notification coalescing (P0.3).
- Documentation home: `docs/internals/api-facade.md` for the design, `docs/features/` for the app-facing surface.
- **Related:** [#147](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/147) — custom layer interface, which depends on S5 of this issue.

title: ios-dev: no live-config channel, so every check costs a relaunch

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
`scripts/android-dev` can change any knob on a **running** demo:

```sh
adb shell am broadcast -a com.massifmaps.MassifDemo.CONFIG --es fog false
adb shell am broadcast -a com.massifmaps.MassifDemo.CONFIG --es apiSet fogOptions.rangeStart=2.5
```

`scripts/ios-dev` has no equivalent. Launch arguments are read once at startup, so every iOS check is a **full relaunch** — install, boot, wait for tiles to settle, read the log. Roughly 35 s per data point against about 1 s on Android.

## Why it matters beyond convenience

The reason `DemoLive` exists on Android is written in its own header comment: *a relaunch rebuilds every cache, which is exactly what hides a stale-redraw bug.* Anything about whether a change reaches the drape bake, the shadow mask and the sky **in the same frame** is invisible if the only way to apply it is to start over.

It also blocks A/B work on iOS: two values of one knob, same tile set, same camera, is the method the render debugging in [`docs/internals/rendering/`](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/) depends on.

Concretely felt while building the facade API ([#146](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/146)): the Android result-code matrix for `set`/`get` was five broadcasts in about ten seconds; the same coverage on iOS would have been five relaunches, so only the happy path was checked there.

## What it needs

A receiver equivalent to `demo/DemoLive.java`, reading the same key names, so a knob reads identically on both:

```sh
adb shell am broadcast -a com.massifmaps.MassifDemo.CONFIG --es zoom 14
xcrun simctl <something> ... -zoom 14
```

No obvious one-liner exists on iOS — `simctl` has no broadcast. Options, roughly by cost:

- **Darwin notification** (`CFNotificationCenterGetDarwinNotifyCenter`) plus a payload written to a file or `NSUserDefaults` by `simctl spawn`. Works on the simulator; a real device needs the payload to arrive another way.
- **A small local HTTP listener in the demo**, debug builds only. `curl localhost:PORT/config?zoom=14` works on the simulator and, over USB forwarding, on a device. Most flexible, largest surface.
- **A watched file** in the app container, polled or via `DispatchSource`. `simctl get_app_container` gives the path, so a shell one-liner can write it. Simplest, and polling is ugly.

I would take the watched file first: it is small, it works on the simulator today, and it needs no networking permission.

## Notes

- Debug builds only, whichever mechanism — none of this should exist in a shipped app.
- The key names must match `DemoConfig` exactly, or the two demos stop being comparable, which is the point of the file-for-file mirroring described in [`scripts/ios-dev/README.md`](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/scripts/ios-dev/README.md).

title: 3D buildings: soft edges, ambient occlusion, real facade lighting, roof shapes

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body: Our 3D buildings read as flat, pasted-on blocks with hard 90° edges next to Mapbox GL JS's. Close the gap: contact ambient occlusion on the ground, bevelled edges, a per-fragment material with a real facade gradient, and OSM building parts / roof shapes instead of one flat extrusion per footprint. ## The gap, item by item Caveat: our reference shot is a grey style at flat ambient, theirs is a dusk style with a strong directional light. Part of the difference is configuration, not code — A/B at the same sun hour before charging it all to the renderer. What is genuinely missing: | Gap | Mapbox property | Ours today | |---|---|---| | Contact darkening on the ground around each footprint | `fill-extrusion-ambient-occlusion-ground-radius` (3 m), `-ground-attenuation` (0.69) | **nothing** — buildings sit on an unmodified ground, which is why they read as pasted on | | Soft / bevelled vertical and roof edges | `fill-extrusion-edge-radius`, `fill-extrusion-rounded-roof` (default `true`) | hard 90°; `tesselatePolygon3D` emits raw walls | | Facade gradient over the whole wall | `fill-extrusion-vertical-gradient` (default `true`), `-ambient-occlusion-radius` | exists, but as `1 - 0.65/(1+h²)` in **absolute metres**, evaluated **per vertex** — dead above ~2 m, so a tall facade is flat | | Lit windows / emissive at night | `fill-extrusion-emissive-strength` | none | | Wall-vs-roof tonal separation | their 3D lighting mode | one Lambert term; roofs fall back to **view-direction** lighting on the legacy path | | Complex buildings — parts, roof shapes | `building` layer parts | one extrusion per footprint, flat roof | | Stipple artifact on tall walls | — | shadow acne. A bug, not a missing feature | ## Plan **Track 0 — renderer refactor** (~2-3 d, own PR, zero behaviour change) — shared with #131: - `begin3DPass()` / `end3DPass()` extracted from `renderGeometry3D`, the per-covered-tile walk extracted from `renderShadowCasters`, and `renderTileGeometry` split into common uniform setup vs vertex-layout binding. - One `applyLighting3D(color, normal, normalizedHeight, sideVertex, ao, emissive)` contract that extrusions **and** 3D models call, so a model and the wall beside it agree under the same sun. - Done when: A/B screenshot at a building camera is pixel-identical. **A4 — shadow acne on walls** (~1-2 d). A bug and the cheapest item, so it goes first. Isolate before touching any constant; the caster-offset reasoning is in [08-lighting-sky-fog.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/08-lighting-sky-fog.md). **A1 — per-fragment material** (~2-3 d). A normalized wall-height varying (0 at base → 1 at roof), an AO term over a radius in metres, a roof-edge term, emissive. New `Polygon3DStyle` fields plus CartoCSS `building-vertical-gradient`, `building-ao-intensity`, `building-ao-radius`, `building-emissive-strength`. Defaults reproduce the current look, so no app changes on upgrade. **A2 — edge radius / rounded roof** (~3-4 d). The "less sharp sides". Geometry work in `tesselatePolygon3D`: inset roof ring plus a bevel band, with shader displacement along an edge-distance attribute. Roughly +30 % roof vertices. Biggest single visual delta of the set. **A3 — ground ambient occlusion** (~3-5 d). Design decision to make first: bake it into the per-tile **drape** texture (orthographic, footprints already known, free at draw time) or add a ground-effect draw in the 3D pass. The drape is cheaper and fits our architecture; mapbox uses a scene pass because they have no drape. 3D models get contact darkening from whichever we pick — without it a model floats exactly the way our buildings do now. **A5 — building parts and roof shapes** (~5-8 d). OSM `building:part` features with their own base/height, and generated roof geometry (gabled, hipped, pyramidal, domed) from OSM roof tags. Partly a tile-data question — the parts have to survive into the vector tiles — and partly tesselator work. Scope to be split once A1-A3 have landed. ## Order and budget Track 0 → A4 → A1 → A2 → A3 → A5. Roughly **17-25 dev days**; all estimates, nothing measured. Each of A1, A2, A3 lands as one measured PR with a [performance-log](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/performance-log.md) entry at the city camera: per-fragment lighting, +30 % roof vertices and a ground-AO pass all cost fill, and city is already the tight camera (27 fps after the last perf round). ## Notes - **mapbox-gl-js v3 is licensed under the Mapbox TOS, not BSD.** Architecture and property semantics are a reference; no code or shaders are copied. tangram-ng, our usual reference, has none of these effects. - New style properties default to the current behaviour, so upgrading an app changes nothing until it opts in. - Documentation ships in the same commits, mostly in [08-lighting-sky-fog.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/08-lighting-sky-fog.md) and [11-tangram-diff.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/11-tangram-diff.md), plus a `docs/features/` page for the new CartoCSS properties. ## Related - #131 — 3D models from a data source. Shares Track 0, the lighting contract, and the ground AO from A3.

title: Custom layer interface: let an app draw into the map's 3D scene without forking the SDK

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
Apps want to draw their own content inside the map — a proprietary mesh renderer, a heatmap, particles, an AR overlay, a custom data visualisation — positioned in the map's world space and depth-tested against the terrain and the tile content.

Today the only route is a C++ `Layer` subclass compiled **into** the SDK build. That pins the app to the SDK's exact compiler, STL and internal headers, and every renderer refactor is a breaking change for them. In practice nobody does it.

This proposes a **narrow, versioned draw contract** — the shape mapbox proved with `CustomLayerInterface` — reached over the C ABI from [#146](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/146), and over a SWIG director for Java/Swift.

Split out of [#146](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/146), where custom *data sources* are already scoped (P8) and are easy. Custom *layers* are not, for the reasons below.

## Why this is not just "expose `Layer`"

`Layer`'s actual interface is deeply internal ([Layer.h:213–242](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/layers/Layer.h#L213)):

```cpp
virtual void offsetLayerHorizontally(double offset) = 0;
virtual bool onDrawFrame(float deltaSeconds, BillboardSorter&, const ViewState&) = 0;
virtual bool onDrawFrame3D(float deltaSeconds, BillboardSorter&, const ViewState&);
virtual void calculateRayIntersectedElements(const cglib::ray3<double>&, const ViewState&,
                                             std::vector<RayIntersectedElement>&) const = 0;
```

Publishing that publishes `ViewState`, `BillboardSorter`, `CullState`, `RayIntersectedElement` and `cglib` — all internal C++ types, all things we change freely today.

Worse, a layer is not just a draw call. It participates in machinery a plugin cannot be handed raw:

- **The terrain prelude.** Before any layer draws, each `TileLayer` is given `setTerrainRenderOrder`, `setTerrainGroundTiles`, an **ordinal base** and the stack's **ordinal span** ([01-frame.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/01-frame.md)).
- **The depth model.** Content carries `(proxy − layer) × (2⁻¹⁹·w + depth_shift)`, and the total budget is **measured at 0.2** — 0.3 already opens see-through wedges through ridges on device ([05-depth-model.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/05-depth-model.md)). A plugin drawing at raw depth will either z-fight or punch through the terrain, and it will look like an SDK bug.
- **Post-processing.** With an effect attached the whole scene renders into an **offscreen FBO**, and opted-out layers draw into a *secondary* colour attachment sharing the same depth buffer ([14-post-process.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/14-post-process.md)). A plugin that assumes framebuffer 0 breaks the peak-finder look.

So the contract has to hand over exactly what a plugin needs to be correct, and nothing else.

## The good news: ANGLE means GL ES is the right contract

The SDK renders through **one** API surface — `GLES2/gl2.h` + `gl2ext.h`, ~1730 call sites over 114 entry points — and reaches Metal, D3D and Vulkan **through ANGLE**, already shipping on UWP and Mac Catalyst ([16-graphics-api-migration.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/16-graphics-api-migration.md)).

A **GL ES 3.0** custom-layer contract therefore does not block the Metal path: the plugin's GL is translated by the same ANGLE the SDK itself goes through. No Metal-specific variant is needed now, and adding one later does not invalidate this one.

## Existing precedents in the tree

Two extension points already let apps supply rendering code, and both inform this design:

- **`PostProcessEffect`** ([PostProcessEffect.h:48](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/all/native/renderers/PostProcessEffect.h#L48)) — an app hands over a fragment shader plus named float/colour parameters. Full-screen only, no geometry.
- **`SkyOptions::setShaderSource`** — an app replaces the sky body; the SDK's wrapper declares `u_sunDir`/`u_fogColor`/… and a `fogAmount(rayDir)` helper. **Redeclaring any of them is a compile error and the renderer silently falls back to the built-in sky.** That silent fallback is a trap this contract must not repeat — a plugin whose shader fails to compile has to report an error, not quietly draw nothing.

## Two variants — decide before building

**A — 2D screen-space overlay.** Drawn after everything, no depth participation. The plugin gets the viewport and a `mm_map_to_screen` helper. Covers heatmaps, annotations, HUD, custom labels — which is what most apps asking for this actually want. Cheap and low-risk.

**B — 3D in-scene.** Drawn inside `drawLayers` at the layer's stack position, depth-tested against terrain and tile content. Covers meshes, volumes, AR. This is the one that carries all the risk above.

They are not exclusive; A is a strict subset of B's plumbing. **Recommendation: ship A first**, then B.

## Proposed contract

```c
typedef struct {
  uint32_t size;                                  // vtable version — grows, never reorders
  void (*on_added)       (void* ud, mm_map m);
  void (*on_removed)     (void* ud, mm_map m);
  void (*on_context_lost)(void* ud);              // GL objects are gone, recreate lazily
  void (*render)         (void* ud, const mm_render_params* p);
  int  (*hit_test)       (void* ud, const double ray_origin[3], const double ray_dir[3],
                          double* out_t, uint64_t* out_feature);   // optional, may be NULL
  void (*destroy)        (void* ud);
} mm_custom_layer_vtable;

typedef struct {
  uint32_t size;
  double   mvp[16];              // world -> clip, double: the SDK works in doubles
  float    mvp_local[16];        // same, pre-reduced to `origin` — ready for a uniform, no jitter
  double   origin[3];            // world origin that mvp_local is relative to
  int      viewport[4];
  double   camera_pos[3];        // lon, lat, altitude
  float    zoom, tilt, rotation, fov_y, near_plane, far_plane;
  float    depth_ordinal_base;   // this layer's slice of the stack's depth budget
  float    depth_ordinal_span;
  float    depth_shift;          // the terrain depth_shift resolved for THIS frame
  uint32_t framebuffer;          // the currently bound FBO — NOT necessarily 0
  double   delta_seconds;
} mm_render_params;
```

Registered like any other type from [#146](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/146):

```java
map.addLayer("mymesh", "{'type':'custom','opacity':0.8}");   // ordering, visibility, opacity as usual
```

### The five rules a plugin must follow

1. **Use `mvp_local`, not `mvp`, for vertex transforms.** A float matrix at world scale jitters; the origin-relative one does not. `mvp` is there for CPU-side math that needs the precision.
2. **Apply the depth ordinal in your vertex shader**, or you z-fight and punch through terrain. The header ships the exact GLSL snippet — same pattern as the sky wrapper, but with a **hard compile error surfaced to the app**, never a silent fallback.
3. **Render into `p->framebuffer`.** Never `glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0)` — with a post-process effect attached the scene is offscreen.
4. **Restore GL state.** Explicit list in the header: program, **VAO**, active texture unit and bindings, blend enable + func, depth test/write/func, cull face, viewport, scissor. VAO is the sharp edge — the SDK binds VAOs per program, and a plugin leaving one bound corrupts the *next* layer, which reads as an SDK bug rather than a plugin bug.
5. **Do not request a redraw unconditionally.** `mm_request_redraw(map)` exists for animation, but the renderer is not free-running; a plugin asking every frame is an endless render loop that presents as battery drain, not as a bug ([01-frame.md](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/01-frame.md)). The double-buffer rule applies too — one requested frame does not change what is on screen.

`render` is called on the **GL render thread**, inside `drawLayers`. It must not block; uploads go there or through the plugin's own thread plus a fence.

### Java / Swift

The C vtable is the definition. Java and Swift get a narrow SWIG director class exposing the same five callbacks with `mm_render_params` as a value type — no `ViewState`, no `BillboardSorter`, no cglib. Same contract, different binding, exactly as mapbox does it.

## Risks, stated plainly

- **It freezes part of the renderer.** [#132](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/132) Track 0 is already extracting `begin3DPass()`/`end3DPass()`. A public draw hook constrains that. Mitigation: the `size` field on both structs, a documented "params struct grows, never reorders" rule, and exposing only the three depth scalars rather than the terrain cover or ordinal machinery.
- **A misbehaving plugin looks like an SDK bug.** Unrestored GL state corrupts the *following* layer. This is why C3 below (a debug-build state guard) is not optional.
- **ANGLE gaps are iOS-only failures.** A plugin using an extension ANGLE does not implement works on Android and fails on iOS. The documented contract is plain ES 3.0, nothing beyond.
- **iOS plugins are compile-time linked**, same as the plugin API note in [#146](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/146). Dynamic loading of third-party code is App Store-hostile.

## Plan

- **C0 — decide A / B / both** (decision, no code)
- **C1 — 2D screen-space overlay** (~4 d): vtable, state save/restore, `mm_map_to_screen` helper, demo layer
- **C2 — 3D in-scene** (~6 d): ordinal slice, depth GLSL snippet in the header with a real compile error, double/float MVP pair, FBO contract
- **C3 — GL state guard** (~2 d): debug build asserts the plugin restored every documented piece of state, at the boundary, so a violation is attributed to the plugin
- **C4 — picking hook** (~3 d): `hit_test` routed through the normal `MapEventListener` path
- **C5 — docs + demo** (~3 d): `docs/internals/rendering/17-custom-layer.md`, a `docs/features/` page, and a working custom layer in `scripts/android-dev`

Roughly **18 dev days**; all estimates, nothing measured.

**Depends on [#146](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/issues/146) P4** — the C ABI, the handle table and vtable versioning. C1 is not startable before that lands.

## Notes

- **mapbox-gl-js v3 is licensed under the Mapbox TOS, not BSD.** `CustomLayerInterface`'s *shape* is a reference; no code is copied.
- Opt-in and additive. Nothing changes for existing apps.
- tangram-ng has no equivalent extension point, so there is no reference implementation to copy here — unusually for this project.

title: 3D models: draw GLB meshes from a data source, styled in CartoCSS

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Planned work, shown on the website roadmap page

body:
Place glTF/GLB 3D models from any data source — a GeoJSON file, an MVT layer — and style them in CartoCSS, the way markers and buildings already are. Many instances per tile, lit, fogged and shadowed by the same 3D scene as the extrusions next to them.

![Mapbox GL JS: 3D models placed from a GeoJSON source](https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/assets/ideal-img/add-3d-models-using-geojson-source.2832262.960.png)

*Target: [Mapbox GL JS — add 3D models using a GeoJSON source](https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/example/add-3d-models-using-geojson-source/). Image © Mapbox, hotlinked from their docs — replace with our own screenshot once we render this.*

## Why the tile path, not a vector element

The SDK already draws models: `NMLModel` + `NMLModelStyle`, drawn per element by `BillboardRenderer::drawNMLBatch`. That path has no CartoCSS, no tile streaming, no terrain drape, and does not participate in the shadow-caster pass.

Going through the tile path instead — a `model` symbolizer, fed by `GeoJSONVectorTileDataSource` like any other layer — buys all of it for free: per-feature expressions for rotation/scale/colour, tile culling, GPU draping on the terrain, fog, and shadows.

## What already exists

| Piece | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Mesh + material + texture GL drawing | `libs-massif/nml/` (`GLModel`, `GLSubmesh`, `GLMaterial`, `GLTexture`) | ships today, ES2, phong/lambert |
| Point-symbolizer → tile content, asset resolved by name | `MarkersSymbolizer` + `vt::BitmapManager` + `VTBitmapLoader` | the template for `ModelSymbolizer` / `ModelManager` |
| CartoCSS → symbolizer plumbing | `CartoCSSMapnikTranslator` (`building` is the closest analogue) | works |
| Shadow caster pass, cascades, receiver PCF | `GLTileRenderer::renderShadowCasters` | tile layers only — models hook into the same walk |
| GPU drape (vertex z from the elevation texture) | `GLTileRendererShaders.h` | model anchors drape the same way, with no CPU re-bake |
| 3D pass: overlay FBO, terrain-occluder depth seed, extrusion depth slack | `GLTileRenderer::renderGeometry3D` | models must draw **inside** it or they will not occlude buildings correctly |

Missing entirely: any glTF/GLB parser, any mesh geometry type in `vt`, instancing.

## Plan

Assumes the **OpenGL ES 3.0 baseline** ([graphics API migration](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/rendering/16-graphics-api-migration.md), Phase 2) has landed — instancing then is core, so there is one draw path and no ES2 fallback. UWP's `EGLContextWrapper` hardcodes client version 2 and must be flipped, or models silently do not run there.

**Phase 0 — renderer refactor** (~2-3 d, own PR, zero behaviour change; shared with the buildings work)

- `begin3DPass()` / `end3DPass()` extracted from `renderGeometry3D`: overlay-vs-inline decision, terrain-occluder depth seeding, extrusion depth-bias regime, composite.
- Extract the per-covered-tile walk from `renderShadowCasters` so a second caster kind hooks in.
- Split `renderTileGeometry` into common uniform setup (terrain / lighting / shadow / fog / blend) and vertex-layout binding, removing the `type != POLYGON3D` branch thicket.
- One `applyLighting3D(...)` contract that extrusions **and** models call, so a model and the wall beside it agree under the same sun.
- Done when: A/B screenshot at a building camera is pixel-identical.

**Phase 1 — GLB loader** (~3-5 d)

- `vt::Model`: plain struct — meshes (interleaved pos/normal/uv, `uint32` indices), materials (baseColor factor + texture, alphaMode, doubleSided), node transforms pre-flattened, bbox. Not `nml::Model`: that is protobuf, in another module, with a different material model.
- `vt::ModelManager` + `ModelLoader` interface in `vt`; `VTModelLoader` in `all/native` does the fetching (AssetPackage / HTTP / file), parses with **cgltf (MIT)** vendored into `libs-external`, decodes PNG/JPEG with the existing decoders. `vt` gains no new dependency.
- Scope: static meshes, baseColor + texture. No skinning, animation, Draco, KTX2 or meshopt in this phase — first task is checking whether the reference assets need any of them.
- Done when: `tower.glb` and `wind_turbine_static.glb` load on device and one instance is visible through the existing `NMLModel` path — no new render code yet.

**Phase 2 — CartoCSS + tiles + instanced draw + shadows** (~8-10 d)

- `ModelSymbolizer` in mapnikvt + translator entries: `model-file`, `model-scale`, `model-rotation`, `model-translate`, `model-color`, `model-opacity`. All expressions, so per-feature rotation/scale from GeoJSON properties is free.
- `ModelStyle` in `vt/Styles.h`; `TileLayer` gains `TileModelInstances` (model ref + packed instance array + feature ids) — a sibling of `TileGeometry`, not a new geometry type, since instances are not triangles.
- Instance record, 32 B: `vec4 posScale` (tile-local x, y, z offset, uniform scale) + `vec4 rot` (quaternion as normalized shorts) + `vec4 color` (RGBA8), divisor 1. One `glDrawElementsInstanced` per (tile, model, material), inside Phase 0's 3D pass.
- Terrain: the instance anchor is draped **in the vertex shader** from the elevation texture. Deliberate divergence from mapbox, who bake DEM z on the CPU and re-bake when exaggeration changes.
- Shadows: a `modelshadow` caster program reusing the instance attributes; receiving comes free from the existing `shadowReceiverFlags()` program factory, as do fog and the app's custom 3D lighting shader.
- Done when: a GeoJSON source plus a CartoCSS `model` rule puts N models on 3D terrain at a stated camera; they occlude and are occluded by buildings, cast shadows on the ground and on each other, and fog correctly.

**Phase 3 — scale and polish** (~4-6 d)

- Density reduction on mapbox's model (per-tile lookup grid, coarser at low zoom, off at z18+), opt-out.
- Far/near cutoff opacity fades; LOD (a GLB per zoom band).
- Picking: ray vs instance OBB.
- Transparent materials: back-to-front sort, two-pass when opacity < 1.
- Bench entry in [performance-log](https://github.com/massif-maps/MassifMaps/blob/master/docs/internals/performance-log.md): fps vs instance count at the city camera, on an Adreno 610.

## Cost and risks

Roughly **17-24 dev days** for the four phases, on top of the ES3 baseline. All estimates, nothing measured.

- Binary size: cgltf + the model renderer, estimated +150-250 KB per ABI, **unmeasured**. Should sit behind a `sdk_profiles.json` profile so apps that do not want models do not pay.
- PBR → our phong lighting is a downgrade; output will not match a mapbox screenshot exactly.
- Texture memory across many distinct models needs an LRU in `ModelManager`.
- **mapbox-gl-js v3 is licensed under the Mapbox TOS, not BSD.** It is an architecture reference only — no code, no shaders copied. Permissive references: cgltf (MIT), Cesium (Apache-2). tangram-ng, our usual reference, has no model support at all.

## Related

Documentation lands in the same commits: a new `docs/internals/rendering/17-models.md`, entries in both rendering index tables, a `docs/features/` page for the CartoCSS properties, and doc comments in `all/modules/*.i`.

- #132 — 3D buildings look upgrade. Shares Phase 0, the `applyLighting3D` contract, and the ground AO that keeps a model from floating.
